source.reason: General fully-austenitic solution-treated condition for Fe-30Mn-9Al steels, applicable to this solution-treated 2.7% Si sample.
High-Mn (30%) high-Al (9%) steels solution treated above 950°C are fully austenitic; this sample was solution treated at 1100°C.
The steel is described as fully austenitic, indicating a single austenite phase.
Solution-treated fully austenitic matrix of the 2.7% Si steel.
Fully austenitic steel after solution treatment above 950°C.
Average grain size of 50 µm is reported for the hot-rolled Fe-30Mn-9Al-2.7Si-0.9C steel (as-hot-rolled parent condition); the solution-treated grain size is not separately reported.
Room-temperature Charpy V-notch notch toughness reported for the hot-rolled Fe-30Mn-9Al-2.7Si-0.9C steel after solution treatment at 1100°C for 10 min and water quenching.

Solution treating for 10 min at 1100°C and water quenching greatly improved toughness to an average of 160 J (L-T orientation); this is the room-temperature CVN breaking energy, recorded here under fracture_toughness as the closest available slot.
The paper compares room-temperature CVN toughness of the as-hot-rolled and solution-treated conditions of the same Fe-30Mn-9Al-2.7Si-0.9C steel.
Room-temperature CVN notch toughness of the solution-treated 2.7% Si steel is reported.

purpose.value: Measure notch toughness (CVN breaking energy) of the solution-treated 2.7% Si steel

key_findings.value: Solution treatment at 1100°C for 10 min and water quenching improved CVN toughness to an average of 160 J (L-T orientation); fracture was completely ductile.

source.reason: SEM secondary-electron fractographs of CVN specimens of the hot-rolled, solution-treated and quenched Fe-30Mn-9Al-2.7Si-0.9C steel (Fig. 13b).

purpose.value: Characterize the CVN fracture surface of the solution-treated specimen

key_findings.value: Fracture surface is fully ductile: rounded, roughly equiaxed units separated by a network of fine dimples and tear ridges, with no large flat cleavage facets.

unmapped_findings: Baseline for comparison (parent as-hot-rolled condition, not this solution-treated sample): the same Fe-30Mn-9Al-2.7Si-0.9C steel (0.023% P, 50 µm average grain size) had room-temperature CVN breaking energies of 23 J (L-T orientation) and 22 J (T-L orientation), with mainly transgranular cleavage-type fracture; the cleavage facets displayed slip traces at roughly 60° angles from one another, indicating fracture by decohesion of active slip planes.

The large CVN energy difference between the hot-rolled and solution-treated conditions is related to short-range ordering (SRO) and precipitation of j-carbide, because the hot-rolled material was slow cooled after deformation.
